note: Design parameters of the stacking module (step 6.7). Separate catalog owned by the module, like the household catalog, so the residential catalog and the golden packages stay unchanged. Normative values live in data/rules/sdmc_rs_1_7_vertical.json and sdmc_rs_1_7_capacity.json. Version 0.2.0 (stage S1) adds the stair types and their design values, the upper-floor placements, the garage stand-in and the roof-orientation policy. Version 0.3.0 (stage S1.1) compares stair configurations and directions, adds the space under the stair, the receiving spaces at each end and the small-house threshold. Version 0.4.0 (2026-10-09): small house = one room upstairs (client decision). Version 0.5.0 (stage S2) adds the s2 block: zoning of each drawn floor around the stair core (grid, topologies, arrival order, zone door rules, small-zone merge, scoring weights). Version 0.6.0 (stage S1.2, short test) adds the access_core block (main door from the site's entry deck, swing, vestibule, permitted walls, strategies A-D, interior void with skylight, light, comparison by occupied area and route length) and the u_well stair (U with a central void); u_well is used only by S1.2 and is not enabled for S1. Version 0.7.0 (stage S1.2 close): no skylight; U stairs at least 2.5 m wide (client rule K08); arrival and half bath as preferences; selector in three levels; two-level search; stair hall rule.

selection.note: Cells of the area matrix (step 6.6) taken to the stacking layer: rank <= k inside each (lot, household, profile); 'all' takes every ranked (feasible) cell. Stage S1 draws, by default, only the best cell (rank 1) of each (lot, household, profile); the CLI's --cells overrides it.

levels.note: Floor-to-floor equals the brief default (massing_assumptions.floor_to_floor_ft = 10 ft). Ground finish floor 1 ft above grade (slab on grade with an entry step; must stay within the first-story limit of 113.0261(a)). Top-floor plate = 8 ft ceiling + 1 ft roof framing above the top finish floor.

source.citation: Student-defined massing hypothesis for one- and two-story RS-1-7 houses, spaceplan step 6.7 (2026-10); validate with pilot approved plans

roofs.note: A pitched roof spans the short side of the top floor (gable or hip ridge along the long side): ridge = plate + short side / 2 x pitch. The short side of a floor is estimated as min(street-facing width of the strategy, floor area / width) until step S1 draws the floor.

source.citation: Student-defined roof hypothesis (low-slope pitched roofs are common in the Clairemont ranch stock; to be checked against pilot plans)

stair.note: Stage S0 used the residential catalog's stair area (space type 'stair', target area) per level; stage S1 draws the stair from the CRC stair rules (data/rules/crc_2025_stairs.json) with these design values and compares its area with that target.

design.note: Design values at the code minimum (tread 10 in, width 36 in, landing 36 in): the smallest legal stair. Risers: the fewest equal risers at or below the maximum riser of S01. structure_depth_ft: stringer and finish under the treads (10 in), subtracted from the nosing line to get the clear height under the stair.

source.citation: Student-defined stair design at the CRC minimums, spaceplan step 6.7a S1 (2026-10)

placement.note: Every enabled configuration is tried along each joint, in both orientations of its bounding box and the four directions/hands that keep that box, at the positions closest to the joint's middle. A candidate is valid when its footprint lies in the upper and the ground floor and out of the garage, and its arrival zones fit: bottom zone in the ground floor (out of the garage and the stair), top zone in the upper floor (out of the stair opening). The half bath under the stair is searched in the best half_bath_trials placements of each configuration (by the rest of the key); the bottom arrival zone may serve as the half bath's vestibule. Arrival zones wider than the stair are centred on its end or aligned with either side.
placement.choice_note: Lexicographic choice among valid candidates: smallest net ground-floor cost (footprint minus usable space under the stair, in buckets), then a half bath fits under the stair (vestibulated), then the bottom zone closest to the front (entry), then the position closest to the joint's middle.

source.citation: Student-defined comparison of stair configurations, spaceplan step 6.7a S1.1 (2026-10)

future.l_winder: L with winder treads (R311.7.5.2.1): registered as a future option, no geometry yet

under_stair.note: Clear height under the stair = nosing line - structure depth. Space with at least the storage height counts as recovered ground-floor area. A half bath sits in the half-bath band (fixture headroom, S11) and may extend beyond the stair end by up to half_bath_extension_max_ft to reach the half_bath minimum area of the residential catalog; it needs a vestibule square of vestibule_ft beside it (client rule K04).

source.citation: Student-defined under-stair bands, spaceplan step 6.7a S1.1 (2026-10)

below_grade.note: Exposures (grade to the finish floor above) reported per lot to show how the basement rules classify a level -1 on that lot; the basement options B1-B3 are step 6.7b.

upper_floor.note: The upper floor is a band of the ground floor cut parallel to the front (rear or front placement) or a rectangle anchored on the garage corner (over_garage), so it is contained in the ground floor by construction; the first placement in the order that holds the stair is chosen and every placement is reported. Partial upper floors (V4: guest, work) try the room over the garage first. Compact (S1.1): a rectangle at the rear of the ground floor, centred, at least compact_min_depth_ft deep (stair plus arrival zone), for small upper floors where a full-width band would be a few feet deep.

source.citation: Student-defined placement hypothesis (private floor toward the garden; room over the garage for partial upper floors), spaceplan step 6.7a S1 (2026-10)

garage.note: Stand-in garage on the ground floor until stage S2 zones it: a rectangle on the front line, on `side` of the footprint (right = the far end of the front edge in the lot frame, seen from the street); width by area (double from double_from_sqft unless it takes more than max_width_fraction of the footprint width, then a tandem single width); depth = area / width. Its area comes from the area matrix (IC minus the garage-excluded IC, times the FAR base area).

source.citation: Student-defined garage stand-in, spaceplan step 6.7a S1 (2026-10); the driveway side of the site layer is not in the contracts yet

roof_orientation.note: Stage S1 checks the roof of the drawn upper floor against the 131.0444 plane: first the default roof spanning the short side (as in S0), then the same roof with the ridge turned 90 degrees, then the flat roof; the first that stays inside the plane is kept. If none does, the upper floor must step in from the side setback by the reported inset.

source.citation: Student-defined roof policy, spaceplan step 6.7a S1 (2026-10)

geometry.note: Numerical settings of the S1 drawing (bands cut to an area by bisection; coordinates rounded in the contract).

stair_access.note: Receiving spaces at the stair ends (client rules K01-K02). A house is small when its upper floor serves at most small_house_upper_rooms_max rooms (habitable spaces of the private zone, plus study and flex rooms): the stair then arrives into an upper vestibule instead of a hall. Arrival zones: the hall or vestibule rectangle in front of the top step; at the bottom, the landing of the CRC (S05) times the stair width. Option C (kitchen) stays available for every scheme (client decision); the preferred option is what S2 tries first.

source.citation: Small-house threshold = 1 room upstairs (client decision 2026-10-09); arrival zones student-defined, spaceplan step 6.7a S1.1 (2026-10)

topology.note: Each floor is cut into bands along an axis (y: access side / far side; x: along the front) and each band into a row of columns, one zone per column, like strategy A of the zoning module. Cuts are placed where the free area of each band and column equals its target (grid prefix sums), so polygonal floors are handled by clipping.

zone_parts.note: Parts used to split a zone in two (split_zones); without a scheme the rooms are balanced by area.

merge_small.note: A service zone smaller than zoning.merge_options.service.max_area_sqft (residential catalog) joins the first zone listed that exists on its floor (laundry off the kitchen downstairs, laundry closet off the hall upstairs).

circulation_min_sqft.note: Least circulation area on the upper floor by receiving space (arrival zone plus a short hall), used when the prorated halls of the program are smaller.

s2.arrival_note: Receiving space at the top of the stair (client rule K01): the allowed receivers (hall, upper vestibule, family room when upstairs) are all searched; K01's order is a preference scored by the weight 'arrival'. Superseded order kept for reference in arrival_order.

zone_doors.note: Zone-level door rules read from step 5 (rev. 2): private terminal rooms open only onto circulation; the garage opens to circulation or to its service group. Two zones are linked when they share at least zoning.min_contact_ft of wall and the door is allowed.

vertical_depth_ok.note: Steps through the zone graph (stair counted as one) under which a matrix pair whose roles sit on different floors counts as met.

source.citation: Student design decisions 2026-10-10 (step 6.7a S2 plan: core-anchored lightweight enumerator, A/B/C bottom portfolio, K05 over the base matrix); values provisional

facade_sides.note: Facade roles of the zoning profile read on the drawn ground floor: the front (low y) faces the main street, the rear (high y) the garden, the sides are street views.

pair_default_weights.note: Weights of client relation pairs (K05) that give none, as the base matrix does by type.

unit_min_width.note: Least width of a zone unit: the largest min_side_ft of its spaces (space_sides, default) or the zone's min_width_ft (zone, the convention of the one-floor zoning). On the upper floor a social zone of study and flex rooms is not held to the width of a living room.

split_zones.note: Zones that may also be searched as two units (one on each side of the stair hall), split by the zone_parts scheme of s2.zone_parts or balanced by area; each unit needs a habitable room. The whole zone is always searched too.

door.note: Main door on the street facade of the ground floor, centred on the site's entry deck measured from the inner edge of the driveway (the garage side follows the driveway); clear width as the accessible door of the residential catalog; leaf swings inward, hinged on the side nearer a wall.

vestibule.note: Arrival zone behind the main door (client definition step 2); fixed object the circulation zone must open onto.

walls.note: Walls the stair may sit against: exterior side and rear walls of the ground floor that continue on the upper floor, and the edge of the interior void; never the street facade of the door nor the garage wall; the joint (centre) only as the last resort. Structure not considered yet (client decision 2026-10-10).

void.note: Strategy C: interior void between the flights of a U; no floor over it upstairs. No skylight over the stair (client decision 2026-10-10): the void is lit only through a window like the other strategies.

comparison.note: Three levels: hard filters (geometry, door, circulation, light K06, allowed arrival, stair hall); the Pareto front of route length and occupied area; among the front, the candidates within route_tolerance_ft of the shortest route are ordered by the client preferences (strategy K07, arrival K01, half bath K09), then by route and area.

positions.note: Two-level search along each permitted wall: every coarse_step_ft (at most max_positions per wall, nearest the wall's middle first), then every fine_step_ft within refine_window_ft of the seeds_per_wall best placements of each wall and configuration (by occupied area, then distance to the vestibule). The half bath (a preference, client rule K09) is looked for only in the candidates preselected for S2.

source.citation: Client definitions 2026-10-10 (entry procedure steps 0-7; walls; inward door; vestibule 5x5; interior void); values provisional

light.note: A window counts when the landing (else a flight) runs along a permitted exterior wall for at least min_contact_ft where S13 allows openings.

circulation.note: The stair (and the void) may not cut off more than this share of the free floor from the vestibule (ground) or from the arrival (upper): client step 5, no interference with circulation.

stair_hall.note: Stage S2, both floors: the stair borders the circulation zone along at least min_circulation_contact_ft (a full stair width); the open room zones (living, kitchen: no walls inside) take no more than max_open_zone_share of its edge; a single private zone no more than max_private_unit_share (not enclosed on three sides; bedrooms on both sides behind walls are fine). The stair never stands inside a room.
